The OsSUMO1 was cloned into the pET28a expression vector, generating the construct pET28a-OsSUMO1. SUMO1 protein may be produced in two different ways: precursor or mature forms (see Scheme 2). This should be defined during the cloning step by specifying where to terminate protein translation. If the SUMO protein is produced in its precursor form, the C-terminal diglycine motif must be exposed before performing in vitro SUMOylation assays. Producing precursor SUMO1 requires additional purification steps (see step 37 and section OsSUMO1: Maturation). Scheme 2. SUMO1 maturation. In vivo , SUMO1 is produced in its precursor form. SUMO1 precursor is processed by a cysteine SUMO protease. This process exposes the C-terminal diglycine motif, which is required for SUMO1 conjugation to a target protein. If SUMO is produced in its precursor form, the SUMO peptide must be processed. Proteolytic processing of SUMO precursors can be performed in vitro using the commercially available yeast cysteine protease ScULP1t (Li & Hochstrasser 2003) ( SUMO Protease Invitrogen - Thermo Fisher Catalog #12588018 ). This means that SUMO1 and ScULP1t are incubated in an appropriate buffer (e.g., 10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5; 50 mM NaCl; 1 mM DTT) (see section OsSUMO1: Maturation). After incubation, the mature SUMO peptide must be separated from the SUMO protease and the SUMO1 precursor. Therefore, carefully choosing the placement of the His-tag is essential, especially if the ScULP1t is also tagged with a His-TAG. Option 1, C-terminal His-tag: Since the SUMO protease will cleave off the C-terminal tail, which in this case includes the His-Tag, the mature SUMO can be purified by either a His-Trap or an SEC-based chromatography. This means this option is more versatile. Option 2, N-terminal His-tag: This option requires SEC-based chromatography as the step following cleavage. Scheme 3. steps.title: Grow E. coli for OsSAE1/2
steps.instruction: Inoculate E. coli Rosetta (DE3) pLysS cells transformed with pET200-OsSAE1 or pET200-OsSAE2 into 5‑L Erlenmeyer flasks containing 2 L LB (10 g tryptone, 5 g yeast extract, 10 g NaCl per L) supplemented with 50 µg/mL kanamycin and 30 µg/mL chloramphenicol; grow at 37 °C, 180 rpm until OD₆₀₀ = 0.8.

steps.title: Induce OsSAE1/2 expression
steps.instruction: Add IPTG to a final concentration of 200 µM and incubate for 4 h at 30 °C, 180 rpm.

steps.title: Harvest and resuspend cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge cultures at 16,000 × g for 1 h at 4 °C; resuspend the 7.7 g (OsSAE1) or 9.8 g (OsSAE2) wet pellets in 100 mL Buffer A (20 mM KPi, pH 7.5; 500 mM NaCl; 20 mM imidazole) containing 2 mM PMSF, 5 mM MgCl₂, and DNase I (5–10 µg/mL lysate).

steps.title: Lyse cells and clarify lysate
steps.instruction: Pass the suspension three times through a French press at 15,000 psi; centrifuge the lysate at 20,000 × g for 1 h 30 min at 4 °C and collect the clarified supernatant.

steps.title: Filter lysate for HisTrap
steps.instruction: Filter the clarified supernatant through a 0.22 µm cellulose‑nitrate syringe filter.

steps.title: Equilibrate HisTrap column
steps.instruction: Wash a 5 mL HisTrap HP column (Cytiva) with 5 column volumes (25 mL) of water followed by 5 column volumes of Buffer A (20 mM KPi, pH 7.5; 500 mM NaCl; 20 mM imidazole).

steps.title: Load lysate onto HisTrap
steps.instruction: Load the filtered extract onto the equilibrated column using a peristaltic pump at 5 mL/min (ÄKTA Pure system, 4 °C, max pressure 0.5 MPa).

steps.title: Wash HisTrap column
steps.instruction: Wash with Buffer A until the UV baseline stabilises, removing non‑bound proteins.

steps.title: Elute OsSAE1/2 with imidazole gradient
steps.instruction: Elute with a linear 0–100 % imidazole gradient (mix Buffer A with Buffer B: 20 mM KPi, pH 7.5; 500 mM NaCl; 500 mM imidazole) over 20 column volumes (100 mL) at 3 mL/min; collect 2 mL fractions.

steps.title: Analyze fractions by SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Run 10 % SDS‑PAGE on the injected sample, flow‑through and each eluted fraction; stain with Coomassie Blue.

steps.title: Pool and concentrate OsSAE1/2 fractions
steps.instruction: Pool fractions 10–13 (≈3 mL total), concentrate to 3 mL using an Amicon Ultra‑15 centrifugal filter (50 kDa cutoff) at 4,000 × g, 4 °C, in 10‑min centrifugation intervals; no precipitation observed.

steps.title: Equilibrate SEC column
steps.instruction: Equilibrate a HiLoad Superdex 200 pg preparative SEC column (Cytiva) with running buffer (20 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 7.5; 50 mM NaCl) at 1 mL/min, 4 °C, max pressure 0.5 MPa.

steps.title: Inject sample onto SEC
steps.instruction: Inject the 3 mL concentrated OsSAE1/2 pool using a 3 mL loop; load volume corresponds to ~0.5–1 % of the column volume.

steps.title: Collect and analyze SEC fractions
steps.instruction: Collect 1 mL fractions; analyze by 10 % SDS‑PAGE; select fractions 20–24 (containing both subunits at ~1:1 ratio) for further use.

steps.title: Concentrate and store OsSAE1/2
steps.instruction: Concentrate the selected SEC fractions using an Amicon Ultra‑15 filter (30 kDa cutoff) at 4,000 × g, 4 °C; add glycerol to 20 % (v/v); aliquot, flash‑freeze in liquid nitrogen and store at –70 °C.

steps.title: Grow E. coli for OsSCE1a
steps.instruction: Inoculate E. coli Rosetta (DE3) pLysS cells transformed with pDEST17‑OsSCE1a into 5‑L flasks with 2 L LB (10 g tryptone, 5 g yeast extract, 10 g NaCl per L) plus 100 µg/mL ampicillin and 30 µg/mL chloramphenicol; grow at 37 °C, 180 rpm until OD₆₀₀ = 0.8–1.0.

steps.title: Induce OsSCE1a expression
steps.instruction: Add IPTG to 200 µM final concentration and incubate 5 h at 30 °C, 180 rpm.

steps.title: Harvest and resuspend cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 16,000 × g for 1 h at 4 °C; resuspend the 6.4 g wet pellet in 30 mL Buffer A (20 mM NaPi, pH 7.5; 500 mM NaCl; 20 mM imidazole) with 2 mM PMSF and DNase I (5–10 µg/mL lysate).

steps.title: Lyse and clarify lysate
steps.instruction: French‑press three passes at 15,000 psi; centrifuge at 20,000 × g for 1 h 30 min at 4 °C; collect supernatant.

steps.title: Filter lysate for HisTrap
steps.instruction: Filter the supernatant through a 0.22 µm cellulose‑nitrate syringe filter.

steps.title: Equilibrate HisTrap column (OsSCE1a)
steps.instruction: Wash a 5 mL HisTrap HP column with 5 column volumes (25 mL) water then 5 column volumes Buffer A (20 mM NaPi, pH 7.5; 500 mM NaCl; 20 mM imidazole).

steps.title: Load lysate onto HisTrap
steps.instruction: Load the filtered extract at 5 mL/min using a peristaltic pump; recirculate the 30 mL sample 2–3 times on the ÄKTA Pure system (2 mL/min, 4 °C, max 0.5 MPa).

steps.title: Wash HisTrap column
steps.instruction: Wash with Buffer A until UV baseline stabilises.

steps.title: Elute OsSCE1a with imidazole gradient
steps.instruction: Elute with a 0–100 % imidazole gradient (Buffer B: 20 mM NaPi, pH 7.5; 500 mM NaCl; 500 mM imidazole) over 20 column volumes (100 mL) at 2 mL/min; collect 2 mL fractions.

steps.title: Pool selected fractions and dialyze
steps.instruction: Pool fractions 7–1 (≈40 mL); transfer into SnakeSkin dialysis tubing (sealed with clothespin); dialyze overnight at 4 °C against 4 L dialysis buffer (10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 7.5; 50 mM NaCl; 0.7 mM DTT) with stirring.

steps.title: Concentrate and store OsSCE1a
steps.instruction: Concentrate the dialyzed sample using an Amicon Ultra‑15 filter (10 kDa cutoff) at 4,000 × g, 4 °C (10‑min spins) to desired volume; add glycerol to 20 % (v/v), aliquot, flash‑freeze, store at –70 °C.

steps.title: Grow E. coli for OsSUMO1
steps.instruction: Inoculate E. coli Rosetta (DE3) pLysS cells transformed with pET28a‑OsSUMO1 into 5‑L flasks containing 2 L LB (10 g tryptone, 5 g yeast extract, 10 g NaCl per L) plus 50 µg/mL kanamycin and 30 µg/mL chloramphenicol; grow at 37 °C, 180 rpm until OD₆₀₀ = 0.8–1.0.

steps.title: Induce OsSUMO1 expression
steps.instruction: Add IPTG to 400 µM final concentration and incubate 5 h at 30 °C, 180 rpm.

steps.title: Harvest and resuspend cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 16,000 × g for 1 h at 4 °C; resuspend the 9.88 g wet pellet in 50 mL Buffer A (20 mM KPi, pH 7.5; 500 mM NaCl; 20 mM imidazole) with 1 mM PMSF and DNase I (5–10 µg/mL lysate).

steps.title: Lyse and clarify lysate
steps.instruction: French‑press three passes at 15,000 psi; centrifuge at 20,000 × g for 1 h 30 min at 4 °C; collect supernatant.

steps.title: Filter lysate for HisTrap
steps.instruction: Filter the supernatant through a 0.45 µm cellulose‑nitrate syringe filter.

steps.title: Equilibrate HisTrap column (OsSUMO1)
steps.instruction: Wash a 5 mL HisTrap HP column with 5 column volumes (25 mL) water then 5 column volumes Buffer A (20 mM KPi, pH 7.5; 500 mM NaCl; 20 mM imidazole).

steps.title: Load lysate onto HisTrap
steps.instruction: Load the filtered extract at 5 mL/min using a peristaltic pump; recirculate the 50 mL sample 2–3 times on the ÄKTA Pure system (2 mL/min, 4 °C, max 0.5 MPa).

steps.title: Wash HisTrap column
steps.instruction: Wash with Buffer A until the UV baseline stabilises.

steps.title: Elute OsSUMO1 with imidazole gradient
steps.instruction: Elute using a gradient from 0 % to 30 % Buffer B (20 mM KPi, pH 7.5; 500 mM NaCl; 500 mM imidazole) over 20 column volumes (100 mL) at 1 mL/min; then stepwise to 30 %, 50 %, and 100 % Buffer B over the same volume; collect 2 mL fractions.

steps.title: Pool fractions and dialyze
steps.instruction: Pool fractions 8–17 (≈25 mL); place in SnakeSkin dialysis tubing; dialyze overnight at 4 °C against 4 L buffer (10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 7.5; 50 mM NaCl; 1 mM DTT) with stirring.

steps.title: Concentrate and store OsSUMO1
steps.instruction: Concentrate the dialyzed sample using an Amicon Ultra‑15 filter (3 kDa cutoff) at 4,000 × g, 4 °C (10‑min spins) to desired volume; add glycerol to 20 % (v/v), aliquot, flash‑freeze, store at –70 °C.
